extracted.intended_audience: Authors, peer reviewers, and journal editors preparing or evaluating reports of randomized trials
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and peer-reviewing reports of randomized (clinical) trials using the CONSORT 2025 minimum set: a 30-item checklist and flow diagram to ensure complete, transparent reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: CONSORT 30-item checklist (overall)
rubrics_metrics.description: A 30-item checklist of essential items that should be included when reporting the results of a randomized trial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The checklist is an evidence-based, minimum set of recommendations designed to improve reporting quality. CONSORT 2025 includes substantive and structural changes to reflect recent methodological advancements (seven new items added, three items revised, one deleted). Use the checklist to verify that essential items are present; it represents the minimum required content for trial reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flow diagram for participant flow
rubrics_metrics.description: A diagram for documenting the flow of participants through the trial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the CONSORT flow diagram to show enrolment, allocation, follow-up, and analysis numbers. It complements the checklist and provides a visual summary of participant progression through trial stages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title and abstract
rubrics_metrics.description: Identification as randomized trial and a structured summary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report’s title and abstract should clearly identify the study as a randomized trial and provide a structured summary (design, methods, results, conclusions) so readers and indexers can recognize the study type and key findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduction: background
rubrics_metrics.description: Background information that establishes the scientific context and rationale for the trial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide concise scientific background and explanation of why the trial is needed; frame the research question within existing evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduction: objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Clear statement of the trial’s objectives or hypotheses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State primary and, where relevant, secondary objectives or hypotheses so that outcomes and analyses are interpretable in context of prespecified aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods: trial design
rubrics_metrics.description: Description of the trial design (e.g., parallel, factorial) including allocation ratio and any important changes to methods after trial commencement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report the overall design features and any protocol changes with reasons; this enables appraisal of internal validity and applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods: participants
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligibility criteria for participants and the settings and locations where the data were collected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe inclusion/exclusion criteria, recruitment settings, and relevant dates to allow assessment of generalizability and reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods: interventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed description of the interventions intended for each group and how/when they were actually administered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide enough detail for replication, including comparator(s), delivery, dose, timing, and personnel responsible for administration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods: outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearly defined primary and secondary outcome measures, including how and when they were assessed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-specify outcomes and measurement instruments; report any changes to outcomes after trial commencement with reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods: sample size
rubrics_metrics.description: Sample size determination and any interim analyses or stopping guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe how sample size was calculated (including assumptions) and any planned or conducted interim analyses or stopping rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods: randomization
rubrics_metrics.description: Methods used to generate the random allocation sequence and implement allocation (sequence generation, allocation concealment mechanism, implementation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report details of sequence generation, concealment mechanisms, and who enrolled/assigned participants to enable assessment of selection bias risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods: blinding (masking)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether and how participants, care providers, and outcome assessors were blinded to group assignment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State who was blinded, how blinding was achieved, and assess the potential impact of unblinding on outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods: statistical methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Statistical methods used to compare groups for primary and secondary outcomes, including any additional analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe analysis populations (e.g., intention-to-treat), methods for handling missing data, adjustments, and software used; pre-specify subgroup/adjusted analyses where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results: participant flow
rubrics_metrics.description: Numbers of participants randomly assigned, receiving intended treatment, and analyzed for the primary outcome (usually presented with flow diagram).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide counts and reasons for exclusions and losses at each stage to allow assessment of attrition and its potential bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results: recruitment
rubrics_metrics.description: Dates defining the periods of recruitment and follow-up and explanation for why the trial ended or was stopped (if applicable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report recruitment and follow-up timelines and any premature stopping with justification to assess timing-related biases and applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results: baseline data
rubrics_metrics.description: Baseline demographic and clinical characteristics for each group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present sufficient baseline data to assess comparability of groups and potential confounding; tabulate key characteristics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results: numbers analysed
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of participants (denominator) included in each analysis and whether the analysis was by original assigned groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarify per-protocol vs intention-to-treat analyses and provide denominators for all reported outcome analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results: outcomes and estimation
rubrics_metrics.description: Results for each primary and secondary outcome, including estimated effect size and precision (e.g., confidence intervals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report effect estimates with measures of precision and absolute/relative measures where relevant to aid interpretation of clinical importance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results: ancillary analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Results of other analyses performed, including subgroup and adjusted analyses, distinguishing pre-specified from exploratory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly label analyses as pre-specified or exploratory to avoid overinterpretation of post-hoc findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results: harms
rubrics_metrics.description: All important harms or unintended effects in each group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report adverse events and harms with sufficient detail to assess safety; include both frequency and severity where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discussion: limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Discussion of trial limitations, addressing sources of potential bias, imprecision, and multiplicity of analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reflect on limitations transparently and their likely impact on the validity and interpretation of results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discussion: generalizability
rubrics_metrics.description: Discussion of external validity (generalizability/transportability) of the trial findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider the applicability of findings to other populations, settings, and contexts, including differences between trial conditions and routine practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discussion: interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Interpretation of the results in context of current evidence, balancing benefits and harms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide cautious, balanced interpretation consistent with results, limitations, and other relevant evidence; avoid overstating conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other information: registration
rubrics_metrics.description: Trial registration information (registry name and registration number).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide prospective registration details to enhance transparency and allow access to protocol and pre-specified outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other information: protocol
rubrics_metrics.description: Availability of the full trial protocol and any amendments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supply links or references to the protocol to enable assessment of pre-specified methods and outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other information: funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Sources of funding and other support and role of funders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Declare financial and non-financial support and the funders’ role (if any) in study design, conduct, analysis, and reporting to identify potential conflicts of interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other information: open science
rubrics_metrics.description: Open science practices integrated into the checklist (e.g., data/code availability, materials sharing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CONSORT 2025 includes a new section on open science; reports should state availability of data, code, and materials where possible to enhance reproducibility and reuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer use of CONSORT
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendation that reviewers use the CONSORT checklist as a structured rubric to verify presence of essential items in trial reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Peer reviewers can systematically check submitted trial reports against CONSORT items and the flow diagram to identify missing or incomplete reporting and request necessary clarifications from authors.
